title: One Silk Thread, Split 48 Times — Suzhou Embroidery | China Travel Expert
description:
One silk thread, split into 48 strands — each finer than a human hair. Could your eyes even see it?

This is Suzhou embroidery (苏绣), one of China's four great embroidery traditions, with roughly 2,000 years of history. Before a single stitch, the embroiderer splits one strand of silk into fractions — documented down to about 1/48 and finer. In double-sided embroidery (双面绣), matured back in the Song dynasty, the front and back show the same image with the stitches hidden on both faces — the craft is nicknamed "两面光," flawless on both sides.

🧭 Expert Tip: To watch a master split silk in person, visit the Suzhou Embroidery Research Institute at Huanxiu Shanzhuang garden — go on a weekday morning when the studios are quiet.
